title: Levothyroxine treatment of subclinical hypothyroidism, fatal and nonfatal cardiovascular events, and mortality
authors: Razvi S, Weaver JU, Butler TJ, Pearce SH
population: UK General Practice Research Database patients with new subclinical hypothyroidism (TSH 5.01 to 10.0 mIU/l, normal free T4) in 2001: 3093 aged 40 to 70 and 1642 older than 70
funder: Dr Pearce has been funded to work on subclinical thyroid disease by Medical Research Council grant G0500783. Access to the GPRD was funded through the Medical Research Council's license agreement.
authorConflicts: Dr Pearce has received a speaker's fee from Merck Serono.
result: About half were treated with levothyroxine, modelled as a time-dependent covariate. Aged 40 to 70: ischaemic heart disease events in 68 of 1634 treated (4.2%) against 97 of 1459 untreated (6.6%), adjusted HR 0.61 (95% CI 0.39 to 0.95). Older than 70: 104 of 819 treated (12.7%) against 88 of 823 untreated (10.7%), HR 0.99 (0.59 to 1.33). The authors called for an adequately powered randomised trial with vascular outcomes.
